proposals.before: He later served on the staffs of the generals who maintained the east and who guarded the army, became magistrate of Wen, rose twice to governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of colonel director of agriculture.
proposals.after: He later served on the staffs of the generals who maintained the east and who guarded the army, became magistrate of Wen, was promoted twice and became governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of colonel director of agriculture.
proposals.reason: 再遷弘農太守 means two promotions culminating in the Hongnong governorship, not two separate tenures as governor of Hongnong.

proposals.before: After the abdication, Fu Xuan's noble rank was raised to viscount, and he was also given the title of chief commandant of attached cavalry.
proposals.after: After the abdication, Fu Xuan's noble rank was raised to viscount, and he was also given the title of chief commandant of attendant cavalry.
proposals.reason: 附馬都尉 is the office 駙馬都尉 (attendant cavalry), not 'attached cavalry'.

proposals.before: Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Shun elevated five ministers, the realm was transformed through effortless governance because he put the right men in the essential posts."
proposals.after: Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Shun elevated five ministers, the realm was transformed through effortless governance because he put the right men in the essential posts.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English closes the quotation after the first sentence, but the Chinese memorial continues through the following units.

proposals.before: Therefore in the earlier edict I dared to have straight speech and nothing refused, hoping thereby to be able to air ignorance and mend faults, and obtain preservation of high rank.
proposals.after: Therefore the earlier edict allowed daring straight speech and forbade blocking it, hoping thereby to air ignorance and mend faults, and obtain preservation of high rank.
proposals.reason: 敢有直言 invites others to dare speak frankly; it is not the emperor saying he himself dared to have straight speech.

proposals.before: Chen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what your feet have written; the words are rich and the principles sustain; in ordering the threads of government it preserves and values Confucian teaching—enough to block the Yang and Mo schools' flow and evasion, and align Sun and Mencius with past ages.
proposals.after: Chen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what you have written; the words are rich and the principles sustain; in ordering the threads of government it preserves and values Confucian teaching—enough to block the Yang and Mo schools' flow and evasion, and align Sun and Mencius with past ages.
proposals.reason: 足下 is an honorific for you, not a literal reference to feet.

proposals.before: In the early Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed erudite of the heir apparent, and by stages was promoted to right assistant of the secretariat.
proposals.after: In the early Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed xianma (attendant) of the heir apparent, and by stages was promoted to right assistant of the secretariat.
proposals.reason: 太子洗馬 is the heir-apparent’s xianma post, not an erudite (博士) appointment.

proposals.before: Bearing sons is foolish; finishing official matters—official matters are not easy to finish.
proposals.after: Have a dull son and set him to finishing official business—official business is not easy to finish.
proposals.reason: 生子癡，了官事 is the proverb about a dull son handling office work, not a claim that bearing sons is foolish.

proposals.before: The sovereign was in mourning seclusion and listened to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, lacking all propriety, at once played Yi and Zhou, thinking himself secure in possession of all under Heaven—this is why he died to the end.
proposals.after: The sovereign was in mourning seclusion and listened to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, lacking all propriety, at once played Yi and Zhou, thinking himself secure in possession of all under Heaven—this is why he died.
proposals.reason: 「所以至死」states that this conduct brought him to death; ‘died to the end’ invents a false idiom.

proposals.after: Changrong is Xiahou Jun (his style name).
proposals.reason: The Chinese identifies 長容 as the style of 夏侯駿; the literal equation omits that onomastic relation already present in the idiomatic.

proposals.before: I have done nothing dramatic, nor have I broken anyone’s power; why should anyone fear me?
proposals.after: I have been in office some days, yet I have made no striking move, nor have I snapped a wing as a released bowstring would; who then will fear me?
proposals.reason: The idiomatic drops the source image 「應弦垂翅」and invents a generic ‘broken anyone’s power’.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office at fifty-six. An edict posthumously restored his title as colonel director of retainers, granted one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash, and gave him the posthumous name Zhen, "the steadfast."
proposals.after: In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office at fifty-six. An edict posthumously granted him colonel director of retainers, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash, and gave him the posthumous name Zhen, "the steadfast."
proposals.reason: Chinese 詔贈 is a posthumous grant, not restoration of a previously stripped title.

proposals.before: When Yongjia brought chaos he fled to Kuaiji; Prince Langya (later Yuan-di) summoned him as aide on the staff of the general who guards the east.
proposals.after: When Yongjia brought chaos he fled to Kuaiji; Emperor Yuan summoned him as aide on the staff of the general who guards the east.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 元帝 only; Prince Langya is not in this unit and is an invented identification.

proposals.before: Zhi asked to go with Director of the secretariat Wu Mao to listen for news of the state, bowed and went down the steps.
proposals.after: Zhi asked to go with Wu Mao of the secretariat to listen for news of the state, bowed and went down the steps.
proposals.reason: 尚書武茂 is an official of the secretariat, not necessarily director of the secretariat (尚書令).

proposals.before: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting commander of the army of the west of peace, with concurrent regular attendant, leading general of the west who pacifies the wilderness Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.
proposals.after: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting army director of Pacifying-the-West, with concurrent regular attendant, and led General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.
proposals.reason: 安西 is the Pacify-the-West command, not 'west of peace'; 安西將軍 is Xiahou Jun's title, not 'pacifies the wilderness'.

proposals.before: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’"
proposals.after: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’
proposals.reason: Trailing extra quotation mark after the already closed spoken line.

proposals.before: When it came to his accepting remonstrance at Runan and presenting writings at Linjin, occupying a place of honesty and straightness, he had foresight indeed.
proposals.after: When it came to his offering remonstrance at Runan and presenting writings at Linjin, occupying a place of honesty and straightness, he had foresight indeed.
proposals.reason: 納諫 here is Fu Xian's offering of remonstrance, matching the idiomatic 'pressed his advice'; 'accepting remonstrance' reverses the direction.

decisions.reason: 再遷弘農太守 is the standard career formula of two further promotions culminating in the Hongnong governorship, not two separate tenures as governor.
The chapter graph 附馬都尉 is the office 駙馬都尉, commandant of attendant cavalry; 'attached cavalry' is a false reading of 附. CText Jinshu keeps 附馬; Quan Jin Wen writes 駙馬都尉 for the same career step.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及受禪，進爵為子，加附馬都尉

decisions.reason: 玄復上疏曰 opens a memorial that continues in the following units without a new speech verb; closing the English quotation at the end of this first sentence falsely ends the speech.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 玄復上疏曰：臣聞舜舉五臣

decisions.reason: 前詔敢有直言，勿有所距 is the emperor's earlier invitation that others dare speak frankly and that none refuse them, not a claim that he himself dared to speak.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故前詔敢有直言，勿有所距

decisions.reason: 足下 is the honorific 'you' addressing Fu Xuan; 省足下所著書 cannot mean that his feet wrote the book.
拜太子洗馬 is the heir apparent's xianma post, not an erudite (博士) appointment.
生子癡，了官事 is the proverb that a dull son should be left to finish official business; it does not say that bearing sons is foolish.
所以至死 means this conduct is why he came to his death; 'died to the end' is not a reading of 至死 here.
長容者，夏侯駿也 literally equates the two names; adding '(his style name)' is a gloss already given in the idiomatic field, not required of the literal.

decisions.after: I have been in office some days, yet I have made no striking move, nor have I made wings droop at the twang of a bowstring; who then will fear me?
decisions.reason: The original drops 在職有日 and replaces 應弦垂翅 with invented 'broken anyone’s power'. The proposal restores tenure and the image, but 'snapped a wing as a released bowstring would' misstates the figure of birds' wings drooping when the string sounds.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 在職有日，既無赫然之舉，又不應弦垂翅

decisions.reason: 詔贈司隸校尉 is a posthumous conferral of the office; 'restored' invents a prior stripping of the title.
This unit names only 元帝 as the summoner; Prince Langya is not in the Chinese and must not be inserted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元帝引為鎮東從事中郎

decisions.reason: 尚書武茂 is Wu Mao as a secretariat official (尚書), not director of the secretariat (尚書令).
行安西軍司 and 安西將軍 are the Pacify-the-West army-director and general titles; 'west of peace' and 'pacifies the wilderness' are false parses of 安西.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 行安西軍司……安西將軍夏侯駿

decisions.reason: The Chinese speech ends at 吾屬無憂矣; the extra closing quotation mark after the already closed English line is an editorial fault, not source wording.
納諫汝南 refers to Fu Xian's remonstrance directed at Runan, parallel to 獻書臨晉; 'accepting remonstrance' reverses agent and patient.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及其納諫汝南，獻書臨晉

claimRetractions.reason: The unit supplies only 元帝; the extracted English title Prince Langya is produced solely by the rejected translation and has no Chinese support here.
